text.p: Copper extended its recent gains on Wednesday, going above $2,230 per tonne on the London Metal Exchange, while nickel and zinc hit new highs.
COMEX Gold ended unchanged in New York at US$346.40.

Copper prices shook off their midsession blues during more active Wednesday afternoon LME trading, pulling other metals to higher closes. Traders said there was a knock-on affect from copper extending its move above $2,200, and zinc and nickel reached fresh highs for this current bull-run.

Copper's spread premiums firmed again with cash/three months whipping back above the $200 backwardation level. Nearby prompts continue to trade at or near the $23 daily LME limit - a trend seen continuing up to the Feb date two weeks away. Copper prices were up to the $2,240 level by Wednesday's kerb close, up $36 from Tuesday.

Fund interest helped zinc move through the previous high and tough resistance in the mid-$1,170s, although there is further overhead supply stretching up to $1,200. Last trade was at $1,184, just off an $1,190 peak, but up $15 from Tuesday. Nickel momentarily broke above the important chart point of $7,820 on speculative buying, before settling back to close the session at $7,810, still up $125.

Aluminium advanced during the afternoon rings, but again ran into tough resistance above $1,625. Nevertheless the close at $1,632, up from an overnight $1,617.50, suggests that there will be another re-test of $1,640 soon.
Lead inched higher and last business was at $681, up just $3. Tin also crawled higher and finished at $5,860, only $5 up from the overnight kerb.

New York precious metals futures ended steady Wednesday, on moderate volumes, but not before gold fell to new three-year lows. "There wasn't a great deal of activity today, but the gold market still feels under some pressure, despite the decision by Eurostat (the EC statistics bureau) ruling out the use of central bank gold sales to improve fiscal deficits to meet EMU criteria," Chase Manhattan New York managing director, Dinsa Mehta said. COMEX April gold ended unchanged at $346.40 an ounce, but not before posting new contract lows at $344.30.

CBOT wheat ended higher on export talk, commercial buying and short covering, traders said. Nearby March was higher on commercial buying, traders said. Cargill Inc bought 3.0 million bushels of March, traders said and Continental Grain bought one million March. Wheat closed one to 3-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up 3-3/4 at $3.61-1/2.

NYMEX heating oil extended its decline Wednesday after oil inventory data showed higher distillate output when heating oil supply was already deemed ample amid mild weather. March heat ended off 0.86 cent at 63.32 cents a gallon after falling 1.10 cents Tuesday. March gasoline ended off 0.77 cent a gallon at 67.54 cents. March crude ended off 11 cents at $23.91 a barrel. Crude's declines were limited by higher refinery operating rates amid relatively tight crude supply, dealers said.
